title: fix(scripts): read nested exports conditions in check-lean-entry-closure, and refuse unreadable ones by name
body:
Part of #16980 — ⛔ deliberately NOT `Fixes`. This lands options 1, 2 and 3. The half left open is the one the ruling reserved: adding the `@objectstack/metadata/errors` row to `GUARDED_ENTRIES`, which needs a second `ADMITTED_PACKAGES` set and therefore a MAINTAINER decision. The PM decides whether the card closes on this PR.

`scripts/check-lean-entry-closure.mjs`'s `resolveConditions()` handed `exports[subpath][flavour]` straight to `node:path`'s `resolve()` with no string check. Options 1 + 2 + 3 from the card, per the dispatch ruling. ⛔ No `GUARDED_ENTRIES` row is added and `ADMITTED_PACKAGES` is untouched.

Clause-②: no
`scripts/**` only — one file. Re-derived rather than copied: 70 published (non-private) manifests, **zero** ship `scripts/check-lean-entry-closure.mjs` in their `files[]`; positive control, 70 of 70 ship a `dist/` path. So the change reaches 0 published surfaces.

## Before leg — the card's own recipe, reproduced verbatim

Measured on a **freshly created worktree at `origin/main` `c43bac7048`, UNBUILT** (`packages/objectql/dist` and `packages/metadata/dist` both absent). The gate blob is byte-identical to the `854639b311` the brief pinned (`e9370b2db2`), so the brief's line numbers still hold.

```
row    { id: '@objectstack/metadata/errors', pkgDir: 'packages/metadata', subpath: './errors' }
  =>   THREW TypeError: The "paths[2]" argument must be of type string. Received an instance of Object

row    { id: '@objectstack/objectql/core', pkgDir: 'packages/objectql', subpath: './core' }
  =>   returned normally: {"conditions":[],"missing":[
         "@objectstack/objectql/core (import) -> packages/objectql/dist/core.mjs",
         "@objectstack/objectql/core (require) -> packages/objectql/dist/core.js"]}
```

⚠️ The control's `missing` is the deliberate exit-3 PREREQUISITE path on an unbuilt tree, **not** the defect — as the card and the brief both warn.

## After leg — same recipe, same rows, same tree

```
row    { id: '@objectstack/metadata/errors', ... }
  =>   returned normally: {"conditions":[],"missing":[
         "@objectstack/metadata/errors (import) -> packages/metadata/dist/errors.js",
         "@objectstack/metadata/errors (require) -> packages/metadata/dist/errors.cjs"]}
```

The metadata row now reaches the gate's own diagnostics with its targets **named**, instead of never reaching a diagnostic at all.

**The flat control is byte-identical**, and that is measured mechanically rather than eyeballed: `git show origin/main:scripts/check-lean-entry-closure.mjs` was written beside the patched file (same directory, so `ROOT` resolves identically), both were imported in one process, and their control-row results were string-compared.

```
BEFORE(origin/main gate): RETURNED {"conditions":[],"missing":["@objectstack/objectql/core (import) -> packages/objectql/dist/core.mjs","@objectstack/objectql/core (require) -> packages/objectql/dist/core.js"]}
AFTER (patched gate)    : RETURNED {"conditions":[],"missing":["@objectstack/objectql/core (import) -> packages/objectql/dist/core.mjs","@objectstack/objectql/core (require) -> packages/objectql/dist/core.js"]}
BYTE-IDENTICAL: YES
```

The temporary baseline copy was removed; `git status --porcelain` showed only the one intended modification afterwards.

## What a future author now gets for an unreadable shape (option 2)

End-to-end through `resolveConditions()` against a real fixture manifest whose `import` condition is an object with no `default`:

```
THREW Error:
…/thirdshape/package.json declares exports["./errors"]["import"] as an object with keys
[types, browser] and no string "default"; this gate reads a condition only as a path string,
or as a nested condition object whose "default" is a path string.
          entry:   @thirdshape/pkg/errors
          subpath: ./errors
          flavour: import
          ⇒ Either that manifest is wrong, or it uses an exports spelling conditionTarget() in
            this file has not been taught. This gate cannot tell which from here, so it names the
            shape and stops. ⛔ What it may not do is resolve something anyway: a closure measured
            from the wrong artifact would be reported as if it were the right one.
```

`Error`, not `TypeError` — so the refusal is distinguishable from the `node:path` crash it replaces. On acceptance criterion 5 (**the message must be honest**): it names *both* live causes and asserts neither, because from inside `conditionTarget()` the gate genuinely cannot tell a malformed manifest from an `exports` spelling it has not been taught. It does not tell the reader to build, and it does not claim the manifest is wrong.

⚠️ **Deliberate behaviour narrowing, stated because it is not free.** The old `if (!rel) continue` skipped every falsy value. Now only `undefined`/`null` mean "this condition is not published"; `""` and `false` are refusals. No manifest in this workspace has either (measured below), so nothing in the tree changes — but it is a change, not a refactor.

## Negative control — the gate on a BUILT tree, figures RE-DERIVED

Built with `pnpm turbo run build --filter=@objectstack/objectql --concurrency=2` under `scripts/pm/os-verify-lock.sh` (15 of 15 tasks successful; `VERDICT command-exit 0`).

```
✓ check-lean-entry-closure self-test: 22 cases pass (attribution, all three judgements, the
  disjointness wall, two real child loads, both condition spellings plus two refusals, the prerequisite).
✓ check-lean-entry-closure: 2 published condition(s) measured from a real load.
  @objectstack/objectql/core (import): 15 packages, 185 modules
  @objectstack/objectql/core (require): 15 packages, 183 modules
  Admitted set held exactly (15 packages); 6 denied names absent.
```

⭐ Re-derived on `c43bac7048` + this branch, not copied from the card. They land on the card's figures — 2 conditions, 15 packages, 185 / 183 modules, admitted set held exactly — which is the result, not the input.

And the strongest form of "unchanged": the **`origin/main` gate and the patched gate were both run against this same built tree and their stdout diffed byte for byte — identical.**

## Self-test: one case per branch, and the floor ratcheted

New battery `reading a condition`, 6 cases: flat condition, nested condition, absent condition, an object with no `default` refused, a third shape (array) refused, and one end-to-end `resolveConditions()` over a nested fixture manifest. Roster 5 → 6 batteries; `SELF_TEST_BATTERY_FLOOR` **5 → 6**; cases **16 → 22**.

Every mutation below was proved on disk (`grep -c` on the exact anchor text before and after, plus the file's `git hash-object` against its `HEAD` blob) and restored with `git checkout HEAD -- <path>`, verified by an empty `git diff HEAD` and by the restored blob hashing back to `8672f581160c61f80134ea605072ade106d2b850`. The fix was committed **first**, so the restore leg pointed at a `HEAD` that carried it.

**Firing control** — `SELF_TEST_BATTERY_FLOOR` 6 → 7, i.e. above the 6 declared batteries:

```
✗ SELF_TEST_BATTERIES declares 6 batteries, below the pinned 7 — a battery deleted from the
  roster takes its own floor with it.
✗ check-lean-entry-closure self-test: 1 of 23 case(s) failed.
```

**Nonsense control** — the roster name changed to one no case registers under (`'reading a condition'` → `'reading a conditionZZZ'`), the exact silencing the roster exists to catch:

```
✗ self-test battery "reading a condition" registered 6 case(s) but is not declared in
  SELF_TEST_BATTERIES — an assertion attributed to no declared battery is one nothing floors.
✗ self-test battery "reading a conditionZZZ" DID NOT RUN — 0 cases registered, 6 pinned.
  The verdict below would have claimed those cases hold.
```

**Ablation of the fix itself** — `conditionTarget()` reverted to the pre-fix `return value;`. The new battery does not merely go red, it reproduces the reported defect exactly, at the same argument index:

```
TypeError [ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE]: The "paths[2]" argument must be of type string.
  Received an instance of Object
    at resolve (node:path:1272:7)
    at resolveConditions (…/scripts/check-lean-entry-closure.mjs:541:20)
```

## Header (option 3) — the sentence that stays false after 1 and 2

`The table shape is what makes that a one-row change for whoever owns it.` is replaced with what a second entry actually costs: its own `ADMITTED_PACKAGES` set, and a package entering an admitted set moves the ADR-0076 D2 boundary and carries `RATCHET_AUTHORITY_MARKER = '⛔ MAINTAINER-ONLY'`. ⇒ Whoever owns a second entry owns a maintainer decision, not just a row.

## Does option 1 actually cover this repo? (the triage seat left this unmeasured)

The triage comment asked, explicitly, not to assume `.default` exists on all nested conditions. Measured across all 71 workspace manifests with an `exports` map:

| condition value | count | lacking a string `default` |
| :--- | ---: | ---: |
| flat (string) | 109 | n/a |
| nested (object) | 102 | **0** |
| any third shape | **0** | n/a |

⇒ Option 1 covers **211 of 211** live conditions. And because there are **zero** third shapes in the tree today, option 2 is prophylactic by construction — which is why its self-test cases have to supply the third shape synthetically. That is the honest reading of what each half buys.

## Gates run — TEXT, not just exit codes

`node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` derived **31** families from the merge base `c43bac704` (its own change-set derivation, not a hand-written list). All 31 were run and reconciled:

```
Run reconciliation — 31 derived, 31 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN.
✓ dispatch-gates --ran: 31 derived famil(ies) accounted for — 31 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED.
```

Zero non-zero exits across the batch. Named among them: `check:lean-entry-closure`, `check:ratchet-remedy-authority` (it reads this very file), `check:nul-bytes`, `check:self-test-wired`, `check:scripts-symbol-anchors`, `check:pm-dispatch-gates`.

Beyond the derived set:

- **`eslint . --no-inline-config` was run in full, not narrowed** — **6410** files, **0** errors, **0** warnings, on the final commit `9998c82a5e`. No narrowing argument is needed. (For the record, the config states at `eslint.config.mjs:328` that there is no `parserOptions.project` and no typed rules.)
- `packages/objectql/src/core-boundary.ratchet.test.ts` — the neighbouring source-scan guard: **1 file / 2 tests passed**. It names this gate only in a comment; there is no executable coupling.
- Control-character sweep beyond `check:nul-bytes`: `grep -naP '[\x00-\x08\x0b\x0c\x0e-\x1f\x7f]'` on the changed file — no hits.

## ⚠️ What I swept and what I did NOT — this list is not complete

Swept: the 31 derived families, the full repo eslint, the neighbouring ratchet test, the published-manifest `files[]` reach, the workspace-wide condition-shape census, control characters.

**Not** swept, and I am naming them rather than implying clearance:
- The 48 artifact-roster families, 11 wide-population families and 13 pending-changeset families that `dispatch-gates` itself prints as **outside** the derived total. Their silence is a fact about a list, not about these paths.
- Two families that take a value from the workflow (`check-shard-attestation`, `check-test-completeness`) — **NOT MEASURED** locally by construction.
- CI convergence. I did not wait for it.

## ⚠️ Two judgement calls a reviewer should check rather than take

1. **The refusal `throw`s; it does not become a `findings[]` entry.** So through `main()` it still surfaces as an uncaught `Error` with a stack — the message is on top and carries everything, but it is not routed through the gate's own `✗ N finding(s)` report. I kept the existing mechanism deliberately: the shape guard one level up (`exports[subpath]` is not an object) already throws the same way, and the triage seat's advice was to move that existing pattern down a level rather than design a new diagnostic style. Deciding that "this gate cannot measure this row" deserves its own report channel — a fourth judgement alongside pass, finding and PREREQUISITE — is a wider call that belongs with whoever adds a second entry. ⛔ It is **not** the PREREQUISITE path: routing it there would print "run the build first", which is a cause that did not occur.
2. **Line number correction for the record.** The brief cites the header sentence at `:116`; on `origin/main` `c43bac7048` it spans `:120-121`. `RATCHET_AUTHORITY_MARKER` at `:156` is exact.

⛔ **I did not add the `@objectstack/metadata/errors` row and did not widen `ADMITTED_PACKAGES`.** Nothing I measured changed my view that adding it is a separate card and a maintainer decision — and the census above sharpens the price rather than lowering it: the row would resolve cleanly now, which is precisely what makes the *second admitted set* the whole remaining cost.

**Changeset**: `scripts/` reaches 0 published manifests (measured above). If `Check Changeset` reds, I have **not** labelled — that is the PM's `skip-changeset` to apply.
